NEUROKIT

Jul–Oct 2025

Connected study toolkit

I led NEUROKIT, a funded PKM research prototype combining adaptive lighting, music therapy, gamification, and a Bluetooth-connected Flutter app. The team integrated generative AI motivation and text-to-speech; OpenRouter and Prosa TTS generate personalized spoken affirmations.

Team third place (bronze-equivalent) · PIMNAS 38

Connected devices
Live website Project video Source code

Problem

Coordinate adaptive lighting, audio, and mobile controls in a single study-support prototype.

My role

I led the PKM-KC team.

Approach

Connected an ESP32 device to a Flutter app over Bluetooth, with study sessions, audio controls, and generated spoken affirmations.

Key decision

Used an HC-SR04 distance sensor and PWM-controlled MOSFET circuitry to adjust lighting across user distances of 30–70 cm.

Result

The prototype measured 516–553 lux across five test distances from 30 to 70 cm.

Recognition

The team placed third and received a bronze-equivalent award in the PKM-KC1 presentation category at PIMNAS 38.

Prototype and evaluation

Hardware

The 15 × 14.5 × 20 cm enclosure integrates lighting, audio, sensing, and a display.

Mobile controls

The Flutter app controls audio and study sessions over Bluetooth.

Validation

Lighting measured 516–553 lux at five distances between 30 and 70 cm. The team reported an 11.35% improvement in a supplementary Wechsler Memory Scale evaluation. The available records give limited detail about the study design.

Tools and methods

  • ESP32
  • HC-SR04
  • Flutter
  • Bluetooth
  • PWM + MOSFET
  • OpenRouter
  • Prosa TTS
